# Checkpoint AO — Scheidt “Stego” provenance correction

**Date:** 2026-09-21  
**Branch:** `claude/dreamy-archimedes-79k6u0`  
**Classification:** PROSPECTIVE CORRECTION / provenance downgrade  
**Cryptanalytic status:** K4 remains unsolved; no new operational parameter or plaintext letter is added.

## Why this checkpoint exists

Checkpoint AN admitted the surviving John B. Wilson quotation as a medium-high-confidence structural constraint. A focused follow-up provenance investigation did not recover the original Scheidt communication and showed that this grading was too strong.

Historical Checkpoint AN is preserved unchanged. This checkpoint prospectively corrects the canonical state.

## Provenance result

The original Scheidt communication was **not recovered**.

No original email, letter, message header, mailing-list post, recording, transcript, or contemporaneous independent copy of the clarification was located.

The surviving Wilson page:
- labels the underlying September 2004 talk report as unreliable;
- says some portions were later “confirmed directly”;
- preserves the guarded wording attributed to Scheidt:
  “there was a piece relating to Stego, but did not state how or in what context.”

However, it does not preserve:
- the communication medium;
- sender/recipient metadata;
- date;
- subject/header;
- preceding questions;
- following correspondence;
- an independent contemporary copy.

## Correct evidence grade

**C — provenance-limited lead.**

The phrase is useful as a documentary lead but does not meet the project's A / strong-B standard for modifying the authenticated structural constraint set.

## Canonical correction

Do **not** state as authenticated fact:

> K4 contains a steganography-related component.

Instead record:

> **Provenance-limited lead:** John B. Wilson attributes to Ed Scheidt the statement that K4 had “a piece relating to Stego,” with Scheidt reportedly adding that he did not disclose how or in what context. The original communication has not been recovered.

This lead does not authenticate:
- the carrier;
- mechanism;
- stage boundary;
- stage order;
- relationship to the English-masking operation;
- insertion/deletion;
- nulls;
- acrostics;
- grilles;
- binary encoding;
- punctuation/spacing;
- physical layout;
- a period;
- key length;
- alphabet;
- reset;
- recurrence;
- alignment.

## Cryptanalytic consequence

**No new cryptanalytic constraint is added.**

The authenticated constraint set remains unchanged:
- K4 masks exploitable English-language characteristics;
- K4 is more than one stage;
- 24 authenticated plaintext letters remain fixed at the two published runs.

The Wilson/Scheidt “Stego” phrase may motivate provenance work, but it cannot select or promote any finite cipher/steganography family and does not justify EXP-044.

## Next admissible evidence

This lead can be upgraded only by recovering one of:
1. the original Scheidt email/message/letter and metadata;
2. a recording/transcript of the underlying 2004 talk;
3. a contemporaneous independent copy with clear provenance;
4. another high-grade Scheidt source defining the same “Stego” statement or its context.

Until then, treat it as a lead only.
